gaps.sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: He ___ to be the best chef in the region.
gaps.explanation: 'People think he is …' → 'he is thought to be …'.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

gaps.sentence: The whole docklands area ___ (REDEVELOP) at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' signals an ongoing process: is being redeveloped.

gaps.sentence: By the time the reporters arrived, the evidence ___ (destroy).
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle for the action completed before the arrival.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: We're having the kitchen ___ (renovate) next month.
gaps.explanation: Causative 'have something done': have + object + past participle. Professionals do it for us.
